      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.

        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"

        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255

        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80

          title: Telephone number

## Summary

I implemented optional owner `email` support across the OfficeFloor pipeline: present-but-valid emails are stored and returned lower-cased, invalid ones are rejected with 400, and a missing email is accepted.

**Schema / DTO**
- `openapi.yml` — added an optional `email` string (maxLength 255) to the `OwnerFields` schema, so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto`/`OwnerDto` gain `email`, and MapStruct maps it both ways automatically.
- `model/Owner.java` — added the nullable `email` field with `@Column(name="email")` and getter/setter.
- `db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql` — added the `email` column to the `owners` table.
- `db/{hsqldb,mysql}/data.sql` — the positional seed `INSERT`s broke with the new column, so I gave them explicit column lists (h2/postgres already used named columns).

**Pipeline (per AGENTS.md conventions)**
- New `NormalizeOwnerEmail` function — mirrors `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`: leaves a null/blank email untouched, validates a present value against a syntactic email regex, and stores the lower-cased value back on the DTO in place; throws the checked `InvalidEmailException` (→ 400) otherwise.
- New `InvalidEmailException` + `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler` + escalation YAML, mirroring the telephone equivalents (400 with `{"error": ...}`).
- Wired `normalizeEmail` into `owners.POST.yml` (after telephone normalization) and `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` (after validate), and updated `ApplyOwner` to copy `email` onto the entity so updates also persist the normalized value.

**Tests** — `AcceptanceTest` (lowercasing, invalid→400, missing→2xx) all pass, and the full suite is green.

Note: I added email handling to the PUT/update endpoint too (not just the tested POST create), since the spec is phrased about owners generally — this keeps create and update consistent.
